Answer: A
Reason: Figure 3 demonstrates persistent, diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates (white-out appearance) without significant cardiomegaly or focal consolidation, which is the classic radiographic presentation of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS). The progression from earlier images showing patchy opacities to this severe bilateral involvement supports a diagnosis of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema consistent with ARDS.
